description:
Blue Sky Plan is open with a dental CBCT scan loaded. The view is currently set to the default bone rendering.

Your goal is to analyze the patient's pharyngeal airway to screen for constriction.

1. Adjust the Volume Rendering density threshold (or window/level) to visualize the soft tissue and airway (the airway should appear as a dark column surrounded by soft tissue, not just bone).
2. Locate the narrowest point of the oropharyngeal airway (behind the tongue/soft palate).
3. In the sagittal view, measure the anteroposterior (AP) dimension of the airway at this narrowest point using the measurement tool.
4. Save a screenshot of this sagittal view with the measurement visible to 'C:\Users\Docker\Documents\AirwayAnalysis\sagittal_airway.png'.
5. Navigate to the corresponding axial slice and measure the airway dimensions there as well.
6. Save a screenshot of this axial view to 'C:\Users\Docker\Documents\AirwayAnalysis\axial_airway.png'.
7. Create a text report at 'C:\Users\Docker\Documents\AirwayAnalysis\airway_report.txt' containing the minimum AP dimension in mm and a classification: 'Normal (>11mm)', 'Narrowed (6-11mm)', or 'Severely narrowed (<6mm)'.

Starting state: Blue Sky Plan open with 'Airway_Case_01.bsp' loaded.
